Explore W.E.B. Du Bois's 700+ articles from *The Crisis* magazine organized by theme, person, place, or time period.

## By Theme

Du Bois returned to the same interlocking problems month after month across twenty-four years. These thematic pages collect his editorials by subject and trace how his arguments evolved.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**The System**

- [The Color Line](themes/segregation.qmd) (144 articles) — Segregation, Jim Crow, social equality, and the paradox that ended his editorship
- [The Mob](themes/racial-violence.qmd) (134 articles) — Lynching, mob violence, legal injustice, and armed self-defense
- [The South](themes/south.qmd) (90 articles) — Southern governance, the press, migration

**The Fight**

- [Voting & Elections](themes/voting.qmd) (131 articles) — Disfranchisement, party strategy, Black women voters
- [Internal Debate](themes/internal-debate.qmd) (72 articles) — Accommodationism, Garvey, NAACP methods
- [The Mission](themes/naacp.qmd) (51 articles) — Building the NAACP, organizational strategy
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**The Structures**

- [Labor & Economics](themes/labor-economics.qmd) (111 articles) — Union exclusion, cooperativism, communism
- [Education](themes/education.qmd) (78 articles) — Funding disparities, industrial vs. liberal arts, philanthropic control

**The World**

- [Pan-Africanism & Empire](themes/pan-africanism.qmd) (90 articles) — Africa, Haiti, India, imperialism as system

**The Soul**

- [Religion & Morality](themes/religion.qmd) (45 articles) — Christian hypocrisy, Christ-as-Black-man, moral argument
- [Women's Rights](themes/women.qmd) (41 articles) — Suffrage, Black women as political force

**The Artist**

- [Art & Culture](themes/art-culture.qmd) (61 articles) — Harlem Renaissance, "All Art is propaganda," Black institutions
- [Literary Writing](themes/literary.qmd) (36 articles) — Fiction, poetry, satire, allegory, prose poetry
:::

## By Decade

:::::: {.grid}
::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [1910s: The Founding Years](1910s.html)
*The Crisis* is launched. Du Bois establishes his voice on segregation, voting rights, and the NAACP's mission during a period of intense racial violence and World War I.

**Key themes:** Founding the NAACP, anti-lynching campaigns, WWI and the Great Migration
:::::

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### 1920s: Post-War & Renaissance
The Jazz Age and Harlem Renaissance. Du Bois writes on the "New Negro," Pan-Africanism, and the contradictions of American democracy.

**Key themes:** Pan-African Congresses, Harlem Renaissance, Marcus Garvey, political disillusionment
:::::

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### 1930-1934: Depression Era
Du Bois's final years at *The Crisis*. Economic crisis reshapes debates over segregation, self-help, and the role of organized labor.

**Key themes:** Great Depression, economic justice, debates on segregation
:::::
::::::
